title: t7: priority-max over four symbols (2-layer, 2-head transformer)
label: partial: function verified on held-out inputs; circuit localisation not verified (whole model involved)
behavior: Input BOS + 4 tokens from {pa, li, po, pu, pi, re}; the model outputs one symbol at the last position.
summary: All numbers are from the local-full backend (full precision). The model outputs the highest-priority symbol present in the input, with the fixed order pi > po > pu > pa > re > li. A six-line predict() agrees with the model on 400/400 and 400/400 held-out inputs (two unused seeds). At head/MLP granularity no component is inert: each of the four heads and both MLPs loses 33-81% of the logit difference when mean-ablated alone. Layer 0 produces only a weak tentative answer at the last position (logit-diff 2.0 of 38.7); layer 1 does most of the work, with the layer-1 heads acting mainly through mlp1 rather than writing logits directly. Layer-1 heads attend strongly (0.78) to pi when it is present, but do not select a low-priority winner such as pa, so the mechanism is a mixture of selective attention and pooled-symbol MLP computation. Circuit verification did not reach 'verified': the whole-model circuit has no sufficiency null, and dropping the weakest head (1.0) keeps 99.25% accuracy but only 64.6% of the logit difference, below the 70% threshold.

claims.text: The model computes a priority max: output = highest-ranked symbol present, order pi > po > pu > pa > re > li. predict() matches the model on 400/400 held-out inputs in each of two verifications (null agreement ~0.35).

re outranks li: on all 14 inputs containing only li and re (both present), logit(re) > logit(li) by 2.1-9.0. My pre-registered guess of the opposite order was refuted. Margins here are far smaller than the typical 38.7.
Both MLPs are needed: mean-ablating mlp0 leaves 19% and mlp1 33% of the clean logit difference.
All four heads are causally involved: exact denoising patch effects are 0.37 (0.0), 0.37 (0.1), 0.36 (1.0), 0.50 (1.1); joint mean ablation of the layer-1 heads leaves 22%, of the layer-0 heads 25%.

Heads contribute little directly to the logits: layer-0 heads ~0.005 each, layer-1 heads 0.10-0.11 each of the clean-corrupt gap, versus total effects of 0.36-0.50. The answer is written mainly through the MLPs.

Layer-1 heads select pi by content (0.78 attention on the pi position from the last position; layer-0 heads 0.32-0.35), but this does not generalise to a low-priority winner: with pa as winner among li/re attention is diffuse (max 0.39/0.33, not on the winner). The 'attend to the max' story holds only for high-priority symbols; this prediction was refuted.

No head or MLP could be shown inert. Treating the whole model as the circuit passes the threshold checks but cannot be null-controlled for sufficiency; removing head 1.0 from the circuit keeps accuracy 0.9925 but only 0.646 of the logit difference (fails the 0.7 threshold). Ablating the 5-component circuit drops accuracy to 0.49.

limitations: Circuit status is not-verified: the task says some components are inert, but at head/MLP granularity every component carries 33-81% of the logit difference; any inert parts may be at neuron or subspace level, which was not examined.
The priority order was read off input/output pairs and tested behaviourally; ties and the all-identical inputs are covered only by the held-out agreement checks.

The edges mlp0 -> layer-1 heads and heads -> mlp1 are inferred from total-vs-direct effects; no q/k/v path patching into specific receivers was run (one path_patching attempt with an MLP sender errored).
Ablation effects are on logit difference; accuracy is much more robust (0.9925 with head 1.0 ablated), so 'needed for the margin' is not the same as 'needed for the answer'.
How low-priority winners (pa, re, li) are resolved inside the MLPs is not explained.
Attention tests used small hand-built prompt sets (16 and 8 prompts).
open_questions: Which components are dispensable for accuracy rather than margin? Head 1.0 nearly is.
What do mlp0 neurons encode: presence of each symbol, or a partial ranking?
Do layer-1 heads select po and pu the way they select pi, and where does selection give way to pooling?
overall_status: partial / not verified · partial: function verified on held-out inputs; circuit localisation not verified (whole model involved)

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The function is a max under a fixed priority order of symbols. For the two lowest symbols I guess li(3) outranks re(7): on all 14 inputs made only of li and re (both present) the model outputs li.

prediction.statement: model outputs li on at least 90% of mixed li/re inputs

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Layer-1 attention follows the priority order, not just a 'look at pi' rule: when the top-priority symbol present is the low-ranked pa (at position 1, the rest li/re), heads 1.0 and 1.1 still put most last-position attention on that position.

prediction.statement: head 1.0's max mean attention from the last position is at least 0.4 when pa at position 1 is the top-priority symbol
